clue.text: Carries out personal property

definitions.meaning: to effect a plan is to carry it out; third person singular
one's ... are one's belongings or goods

explanation.definitionFit: To effect is to bring about or execute, and a person's effects are their movable belongings.

clue.text: Applies for training

definitions.meaning: to exercise a right or skill is to use or apply it
drills done to train body or mind

explanation.definitionFit: Exercises means puts to use, as in exercising judgement, and exercises are practice drills.

clue.text: The craft of the lot without equipment!

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the fortune word wraps round the gear

parts.note: one's lot is one's destiny, fate
a rig is equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: A craft owned by everyone has no gear on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. 'The lot' looks like everyone, but it is one's lot in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a warship, a type of sea vessel.

clue.text: Weed — taking care, get it out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: carefully pull out the weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' is slang for tobacco; 'out' rearranges CAREGETIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Weed is slang for tobacco, and a cigarette is a rolled tube of it.

clue.text: Rifle fire

definitions.meaning: to rifle is to plunder or ransack
to fire is to dismiss from a job

explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, and to sack an employee is to dismiss them.

clue.text: Calm when bill is found in coat

indicators.note: the bill is found lodged inside the word for coat, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to plate is to coat with a thin layer of metal
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm on discovering an invoice tucked in a coat pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' is a verb here, to cover with metal, not a garment; 'is found in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate an angry person is to soothe or pacify them.

clue.text: Courses favouring light-weights

parts.note: pro means in favour of
grammes are very small units of weight

explanation.surface: Diet courses recommending small portions.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmes are courses or schedules of study or activity.

clue.text: An assumed name one must enter unfortunately

indicators.note: must enter means the numeral goes inside the regret word

parts.note: alas expresses regret, much as 'unfortunately' does
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sadly, a pseudonym is needed to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must enter' puts I inside ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is a false name used in place of one's real one.

clue.text: A girl about ten feels for a six-footer

definitions.note: the definition is plural, the answer singular: one feeler

indicators.note: about means round, so the girl's name goes round the number

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl around ten has sympathy for a very tall person.
explanation.walkthrough: A six-footer is not a tall person but an insect, with six legs; 'feels' is a noun, its feelers, and 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is a sensory feeler on an insect's head, and insects have six legs.

clue.text: Strange point Ireland raised

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A peculiar point raised by the Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EIRE into ERIE in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means uncanny, weird.

clue.text: Observing the old-fashioned turn in before midnight

indicators.note: before places the preceding letters ahead of the final piece
turn tells us the archaic word for 'the' is flipped round

parts.note: ye is an old-fashioned spelling of 'the'
the middle letter of 'night' is G

explanation.surface: A traditionalist goes to bed just before twelve at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn in' wants to mean go to bed, but 'turn' reverses the archaic article and 'midnight' is the middle letter of night; 'before' sets the rest ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing something, here spelt without the middle E, means watching or looking at it.

clue.text: A singer having riches to distribute, right?

indicators.note: to distribute is to spread out, so the letters of these words are dealt out afresh

explanation.surface: A wealthy person has money to give away, and is asked whether that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribute' rearranges RICHESTO into CHORISTE; the R for 'right' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a choir, especially a church one.

clue.text: A woman given sanctuary in church

indicators.note: in places the refuge word inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
a lair is an animal's refuge or hiding place

explanation.surface: A woman is granted asylum inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given sanctuary' reads as one idea, but 'given' is a link and 'sanctuary' alone gives the letters; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Claire is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Coppers accepting notes for just being there

indicators.note: accepting means the coins take the notes inside them

parts.note: pence are copper coins, so coppers are pennies
re is a note of the sol-fa scale; two or more of it make res

explanation.surface: Police officers take banknotes in return for merely turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police and 'notes' like banknotes; in Britain coppers are also pennies. 'accepting' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence is the state of being in a place, of simply attending.

clue.text: Order things — rate is to be changed

indicators.note: to be changed signals that these letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy up: the rate must be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be changed' rearranges THINGSRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten things is to put them in order, to tidy them.

clue.text: The fish plainly wasn't fresh

definitions.meaning: a small silvery fish of the salmon family
gave off an odour, in the British past tense of 'smell'

explanation.definitionFit: A smelt is a small food fish, and in British English 'smelt' is also the past tense of smell, here meaning stank.

clue.text: Consumed by anger — must be restrained!

indicators.note: by means placed next to, so the eaten word goes beside the rage word

parts.note: temper is anger, as in losing one's temper
ate means consumed, eaten

explanation.surface: Someone eaten up by rage is told to keep themselves in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumed by anger' reads as one phrase about rage; 'by' only places the eating word after the rage word.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate describes someone moderate and self-controlled, holding back from excess.

clue.text: For the transport of 1 ac?

parts.note: the answer to 1 across means belongings or property, so a vehicle for carrying property is wanted, punning on a holding of land

explanation.walkthrough: 1 across means personal property, also called an estate, so this is a vehicle for carrying it; the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a British car with an extended rear load space, what Americans call a station wagon.

clue.text: A sociable type, though very green

parts.note: extra means very, especially
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: An outgoing person, even if very inexperienced.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic word for green; 'green' wants to mean naive.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravert, or extrovert, is an outgoing, gregarious person.

clue.text: Pottery keeping recently-manufactured article in reserve

indicators.note: keeping means the stockpile word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a store is a reserve or stock
something just made is new
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Ceramics include a brand-new item kept back in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' splits the reserve word after its third letter to hold the new article.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is a dense, hard type of ceramic fired at high temperature.

clue.text: Sporting people involved in a row

definitions.text: Sporting people involved in a row

parts.words: Sporting people involved in a row
parts.note: reads as athletes caught up in a quarrel, but a row here is a stint at the oars

explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' in the surface, a fight, but means pulling a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarsmen are rowers, people who propel a boat with oars.

clue.text: Drink the health of a high-minded individual?

definitions.text: Drink the health of a high-minded individual?

parts.words: Drink the health of a high-minded individual?
parts.note: a raised glass in honour of someone, punningly drunk in honour of a saintly, lofty person, abbreviated St

explanation.walkthrough: The answer split three ways reads as the words you say when raising a glass to a saint (St), the 'high-minded individual'.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast someone is to raise a glass and drink in their honour.

clue.text: A seaman only gets seafood

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
alone means only, solely

explanation.surface: A lone sailor gets a fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible marine mollusc, a type of shellfish.

clue.text: Stir a breakfast cereal

definitions.meaning: British slang for prison, or a term served there
hot oats cooked in milk or water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like a cooking instruction, which suits a pot of oats, but it is a noun: British slang for prison, as is porridge, meaning time served.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang porridge is a prison sentence, same as stir; it is also a hot oat dish eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Friend accompanying leading journalist turned white

indicators.note: accompanying means going alongside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: pal means friend
ED is short for editor, the chief journalist

explanation.surface: A companion with a senior reporter went pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Paled means grew pale, lost colour.

clue.text: Picture, for example, a great way to get a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means the letters are read upwards, so these pieces run backwards

parts.note: EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
the M1 is Britain's first great motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A picture is a fine way of getting a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get a rise' turns EGAMI round in a down entry. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, its 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or picture.

clue.text: Making the beds could be a start .

indicators.note: could be says these letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Making beds might be how the day begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ASTART. 'Making the beds' suggests housework; beds here are geological layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers of rock, which geologists also call beds.

clue.text: Having nothing to do, take some unpaid leave

indicators.note: take some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: With no work, take some time off without pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means inactive, without work.

clue.text: Beat an essayist like Edward

parts.note: Charles Lamb was an English essayist, author of the Essays of Elia
as means like
Ted is a pet name for Edward

explanation.surface: A writer of essays resembles someone called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb (1775-1834) was a celebrated English essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast someone is to thrash them, physically or with criticism.

clue.text: Handy bar

definitions.meaning: to bar is to shut off or block

explanation.definitionFit: Close means near enough to reach, and to close a road or door is to shut or block it.

clue.text: Sort of cell where a billiard sharp is made to dwell (Gilbert)

definitions.text: Sort of cell where a billiard sharp is made to dwell (Gilbert)

parts.words: Sort of cell where a billiard sharp is made to dwell (Gilbert)
parts.note: quotes the Mikado's song of fitting punishments, where the cheating billiard player is shut in an underground cell

explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado the billiard sharp 'is made to dwell in a ... cell', playing with crooked cues.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground prison cell, as in a castle.

clue.text: Letters are sent — that could be serious

indicators.note: could be says these letters may form another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Correspondence has gone out, and that might be grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ARESENT; 'Letters' only hints that letters are being moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and grave in manner.
